thread:
ash: Heads up — found a suspicious KMS grant in a customer private deployment during a pen test. A couple of service accounts have kms:Decrypt on the customer master key. Need quick triage and isolation steps.

maria: Where exactly did you see it? cloud provider or on-prem shim? paste the policy if you can.

ash: On-prem — Vault-backed KMS shim. The problem looks like an overly-broad k8s -> identity mapping that allowed workloads from a test namespace to assume a role with decrypt rights. Snippet from the Vault policy that looks wrong:

```
path "transit/decrypt/customer-key" {
  capabilities = ["update", "read"]
}
```

and the role mapping: `role: developer-team-*` bound in a ClusterRoleBinding.

doug: If it's Vault, we need those audit logs ASAP: /var/log/vault/audit.log on the appliance + sidecar stdout. Also pull kube apiserver audit logs (apiserver-audit).

samir: :rotating_light: Treat as potential exposure. Recommended immediate steps: 1) revoke the affected service account tokens, 2) rotate the customer key (create new version in transit), 3) snapshot all audit logs to immutable storage, 4) run egress allowlist check for those pods.

ash: I'll revoke the SA tokens now. Quick cmds: 
```
kubectl -n customer-test patch serviceaccount sneaky-sa -p '{"metadata": {"annotations": {"kubernetes.io/service-account.token-expiration": "0"}}}'
kubectl -n customer-test delete secret $(kubectl -n customer-test get secret | grep sneaky-sa | awk '{print $1}')
# For Vault: vault write auth/token/revoke-accessor accessor=<accessor>
```

maria: Also ensure NetworkPolicy blocks egress to non-approved KMS endpoints and metadata endpoints. Example NetworkPolicy to deny egress except to our proxy: 

```
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: deny-egress-unless-proxy
  namespace: customer-test
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 10.10.0.0/24 # internal proxy
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 443
```

That blocks direct calls out to external KMS endpoints.

doug: For rotation we can do a staged approach: create new key version, switch consumers to use new key id in canary namespace, run shadow decrypts for 24h, then cut over. Ops can schedule a maintenance window (prefer low traffic).

sec-bot: Incident created: INC-2024-0721. Refer to runbook: https://wiki.redwood.internal/sec/incidents/keys-playbook and add this thread as evidence.

ash: Questions on audit retention/storage — customer requires 2 years of immutable audit. For on-prem deployments our recommendation is: push copies to central long-term object store (S3/MinIO) with SSE-KMS using a tenant-specific key and object lock enabled. Also enable Vault audit devices with log rotation.

maria: Agreed. Example SSE config for central bucket: `server_side_encryption: AES256` + `kms_key_id: arn:aws:kms:...:customer-key` (or equivalent on-prem HSM key id). Also enforce HSM-backed key material and quarterly rotation.

samir: Checklist before closing this thread: revoke tokens (ash), rotate key (ops + doug), collect & snapshot logs (maria), tighten RBAC (restrict ClusterRoleBinding -> RoleBinding per namespace), apply NetworkPolicy egress allowlist, run CVE scan on auth/Vault components, update runbook with new guidance.

ash: I'll open a short PR to change the ClusterRoleBinding to a namespaced RoleBinding and annotate the change with the incident id. Minimal RBAC patch example I'll include in PR: 
```
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: RoleBinding
metadata:
  name: vault-decrypt-binding
  namespace: customer-prod
subjects:
- kind: ServiceAccount
  name: vault-client
  namespace: customer-prod
roleRef:
  kind: Role
  name: vault-decrypt-role
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
```

doug: Ping me once PR is up. I'll coordinate the key rotation with Dedicated infra and schedule the canary.

ash: Will do. I'll post updates here as I revoke and collect logs. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
